passage:
Mridul: can i tell you something i can't say at home
Reena: always
Mridul: everyone keeps congratulating me about the baby and i keep smiling. but i'm scared
Mridul: rent, the car loan, what if i'm a rubbish dad. and i already miss football weekends, which makes me feel selfish
Reena: that's not selfish. that's honest
Mridul: i don't want to worry Anjali. she's got enough going on
Reena: she probably knows something's up. you've gone quiet, right?
Mridul: yeah. she asked twice this week
Reena: then tell her. not as a crisis. just "i'm excited and scared too"
Reena: you two can plan the money stuff together. and the odd football weekend isn't a crime
Mridul: ok. tonight
(next day)
Mridul: told her. she cried, then laughed, then made a spreadsheet
Mridul: i feel lighter. and more useful

qa.q: What did Anjali make after Mridul told her?
What was Mridul feeling behind the smiles?
qa.a: He was scared and under pressure about money and being a good dad, and guilty about missing football.

qa.q: Why was telling Anjali better than staying quiet?
qa.a: Sharing let them plan together, so Mridul felt lighter and more useful instead of withdrawing.

qa.q: How might Mridul's silence have looked to Anjali?
qa.a: She noticed him going quiet and asked twice, so the silence probably worried her more than the truth did.

grounding: Shows an expectant father hiding fears about money, responsibility and lost freedom, then sharing them and becoming more supportive.

passage: The rains were late in their village near Akola, and Tejas stayed in the fields long after dark. His wife Jaya, heavy with their first child, noticed he barely ate and answered in grunts. At the chai stall he laughed with the others when they teased him about becoming a father, then walked home silent. One night on the charpai, Jaya said, "You've disappeared. Where have you gone?" For a while Tejas said nothing. Then it came out: the crop loan, whether the cotton would fail, whether he could be a better father than his own, how he would miss evenings with his friends. "I didn't want to burden you." Jaya took his hand. "I'm scared too. Tell me. Don't vanish." They decided to ask his brother for help at harvest, and Tejas promised to come to the next check-up at the health centre.

qa.q: Where did Tejas and Jaya talk that night?
Why did Tejas keep his worries to himself?
qa.a: He felt pressured and afraid about money and fatherhood, and did not want to burden Jaya, so he tried to seem strong.
Tejas sharing his worries with Jaya; it let them plan together, with his brother's help at harvest and his promise to come to the check-up, instead of him withdrawing.

qa.q: How was Jaya affected by Tejas going quiet?
qa.a: She felt him slipping away and worried, which is why she asked where he had gone.

grounding: Illustrates an expectant father feeling pride and pressure about money, responsibility and freedom, keeping quiet to seem strong, then sharing with his partner.
